title: Before the First Pour / Lessons with Teacher Cha
role: Six-panel apprenticeship extension to the original six-panel pottery story

characters.teacherCha: Fictional strict, caring Korean woman tea teacher; silver-gray low bun, round black glasses, indigo work jacket

prompts.prompt: Use case: illustration-story. Create a NEW two-panel page continuing an original Korean graphic-novel story, "Before the First Pour". Portrait 2:3, two wide horizontal panels stacked, thin white gutter. No letters, dialogue balloons, captions, signs or watermarks; dialogue will be accessible HTML. Reference 1 establishes HAEIN's exact face, low black bun with side-part loose strands, ivory linen button blouse with rolled sleeves and black apron, and the detailed luminous Korean graphic novel rendering. Haein is an adult Korean woman in her early thirties. This is her FIRST SPRING as a novice in a Korean TEA-MAKING workshop, not a pottery studio. Introduce TEACHER CHA, a fictional strict Korean woman tea artisan in her sixties, short silver-gray hair in a neat low bun, slim round black glasses, a plain indigo collarless work jacket over a gray blouse, charcoal trousers, warm lined face, formidable raised eyebrow. Keep her character design clear for later pages. Modest contemporary Korean tea workshop with white plaster, timber lattice, baskets of fresh green tea leaves, bamboo cooling trays and a grounded iron pan at a work counter; not a palace. White, ink black, pale celadon palette with natural green leaves and restrained warm timber. TOP PANEL medium wide scene: Haein has rushed a batch of leaves in an iron tea pan, holding a wooden paddle with a startled, slightly embarrassed expression; Teacher Cha beside her firmly raises one open hand to stop the hurried movement and points with the other at the leaves, brow stern, mouth speaking a sharp correction. Visible tension and a gentle comic sense of being told off. Both keep hands clear of the hot pan, no grabbing or hitting. A faint natural wisp of steam, no flames or dense smoke. BOTTOM PANEL quieter closer scene at a COOL bamboo tray: teacher holds up a dull browned leaf for Haein to inspect, seriously explaining the mistake; Haein looks down at the imperfect batch with a rueful little pout and attentive eyes, ready to begin again. A small basket of fresh leaves nearby. Make it unmistakably a teacher correcting a beginner learning to process tea leaves. No pottery wheels, clay, industrial machinery, formal royal hanbok, humiliation, tears or physical punishment. Original polished narrative art with realistic dimensional materials and expressive but subtle faces.

Use case: illustration-story. NEW page continuing the approved original Korean graphic-novel comic "Before the First Pour". Portrait 2:3, TWO wide horizontal panels stacked with a thin white gutter. No letters, written words, captions, speech balloons, watermarks or readable signs. Reference 1 is the approved preceding page: preserve EXACTLY the same two adult Korean women, their faces and attire. HAEIN: early thirties, black low bun with loose side-part strands, ivory collarless linen button blouse, rolled forearm sleeves, black apron; learning to process tea leaves, not pottery in these scenes. TEACHER CHA: woman tea artisan in her sixties, silver-gray low bun, round thin black glasses, expressive lined face, indigo collarless work jacket, gray button blouse and charcoal trousers. A modest contemporary Korean tea workshop, timber lattice, white plaster, bamboo trays of green tea leaves, subtle natural warm wood. White/ink black/celadon with natural leaf greens. Same luminous detailed original Korean graphic-novel rendering, fine contours and dimensional materials. No royal luxury, ornate costume, clay, pottery wheel, violence, touching hot pans or magical effects. Strong readable emotional storytelling. This page shows TWO DIFFERENT harvests, as the novice slowly learns across multiple years. TOP PANEL close three-quarter view at a COOL bamboo mat on a worktable, away from any heat: Teacher Cha demonstrates a gentle rolling/rubbing gesture on cooled processed tea leaves with her own two hands, while Haein closely imitates beside her; teacher is firm but patient, eyebrow focused, student concentrating intently. Show the two pairs of hands separately, anatomically correct, four hands total, leaves staying on the mat. BOTTOM PANEL in a LATER harvest: Haein thoughtfully examines a leaf between her fingertips above a shallow bamboo sorting tray and consults a small open observation notebook containing only indistinct non-readable pencil marks. Teacher Cha stands beside her listening, no longer scolding, showing a tiny approving smile as the student explains what feels different. Two small batches in separate trays and a basket of fresh leaves show patient comparison, not a ready-made branded product. Her posture is more assured than the first page, but she is still a student. Medium view showing both faces and the table, subtle daylight shift.

Use case: illustration-story. NEW page continuing the approved original Korean graphic-novel comic "Before the First Pour". Portrait 2:3, TWO wide horizontal panels stacked with a thin white gutter. No letters, written words, captions, speech balloons, watermarks or readable signs. Reference 1 is the approved preceding page: preserve EXACTLY the same two adult Korean women, their faces and attire. HAEIN: early thirties, black low bun with loose side-part strands, ivory collarless linen button blouse, rolled forearm sleeves, black apron; learning to process tea leaves, not pottery in these scenes. TEACHER CHA: woman tea artisan in her sixties, silver-gray low bun, round thin black glasses, expressive lined face, indigo collarless work jacket, gray button blouse and charcoal trousers. A modest contemporary Korean tea workshop, timber lattice, white plaster, bamboo trays of green tea leaves, subtle natural warm wood. White/ink black/celadon with natural leaf greens. Same luminous detailed original Korean graphic-novel rendering, fine contours and dimensional materials. No royal luxury, ornate costume, clay, pottery wheel, violence, touching hot pans or magical effects. Strong readable emotional storytelling. Final page, YEARS LATER. Reference 2 is a finished Charim cup-design reference only. TOP PANEL: Haein, now subtly more mature and confident with the same recognizable face and low bun, independently completes a batch of prepared tea at her own modest tea workshop. She uses both hands to carefully gather and sort dry curled tea leaves in a cool shallow bamboo tray, upright assured posture, calm focused smile. Teacher Cha watches at one side, hands resting, quietly proud and letting her finish herself. No heated pan in this panel. This is competent earned craftsmanship after years of practice, not instantaneous transformation. BOTTOM PANEL: the teacher and Haein sit across the corner of a simple tea table in the workshop's hanok window light, sharing the first tea from the batch. Teacher Cha has a small genuine approving smile, Haein looks grateful and fulfilled. Two small handleless Charim cups, one white, one pale celadon, with the same restrained small nacre-look flower emblem low on the outside and a very thin pearl-like accent near the foot, exactly the product direction in reference2, plain light interior and plain drinking rim. Haein gently holds the white cup; Teacher Cha holds celadon. Simple plain white side-handle tea pot on table, a small bamboo tray of the finished tea in the background. Warm emotional resolution between mentor and apprentice, no gifts, no palace, no other people. Keep the emphasis on the women and the cups, serene pride rather than dramatic celebration.
